author: reek
body: The positive half of the scope check. This opening grants itself FileSystem.Read under "/config/" and reads only inside it, so the scope permits the access and the program compiles.

author: reek
body: The second read is the narrowing case: "/config/sub/deep.toml" sits under the granted prefix, and a scope that admits its own subtree is the whole point -- narrowing is always allowed.

author: reek
body: An unscoped grant covers everything, which is why every program that names no scope is untouched by this check.

author: reek
body: What this test asserts at runtime is that both files are ABSENT, and it used to assert the opposite. file-exists was a builtin whose whole body was `li rd, 1`, so it answered True for every path, and this test's expected output recorded that answer as though it were a fact. The green battery was pinning the bug: whoever fixed file-exists would have found this test red and been invited to "fix" the fix. No disk is attached to this VM and nothing is under /config/, so absent is the truth. The scope check is a compile-time judgement about what this program is permitted to ask, and it is proved by the program compiling at all -- not by what the answer turns out to be.

author: reek
body: Device.Block is declared because asking whether a file exists means asking the disk, and the effect row is where a program says what it touches.
